title: Correct a section in one residue fibre while preserving its values on a zero set
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $y\in |X|$, write $L(y)=L_y/\mathfrak m_yL_y$, a vector space over $\kappa(y)=\mathcal O_{X,y}/\mathfrak m_y$ [def-weil-residue-field], and write $s(y)$ and $f(y)$ for the residue values of sections of $L$ and $\mathcal O_X$, respectively. Let $F\subseteq |X|$ be any subset, $z\in |X|$, $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$, and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ satisfy $s(z)=0$, $f(z)\ne0$, and $f(x)=0$ for every $x\in F$. There exists $t\in\Gamma(X,L)$ such that the section $v=s+ft$ satisfies $v(z)\ne0$ and $v(x)=s(x)$ for every $x\in F$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, proof: affine specialization with W=X; base case, global generation gives a section nonvanishing at the chosen point; induction step, multiply this section by a separating scalar and add it to the old section (old item steps 2, 4 and 6)

proof.text: By [def-sc-invertible-module], $L$ is quasi-coherent and locally free of rank one. On each trivializing open the isomorphism $\mathcal O_U\simeq L|_U$ is in particular a surjection, so $L$ is of finite type by [pqf-def-coherent]. Since $X$ is affine, apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections] to obtain a finite family $h_1,\ldots,h_k$ of global sections generating $L$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, proof, base case (global generation) and induction step (addition of sections); affine global generation follows Tags 01PB (properties-lemma-finite-type-module) and 01IA (schemes-lemma-quasi-coherent-affine).

proof.text: Adjoin $h_0=0$ to that family. It still generates: the associated map from $\mathcal O_X\oplus\mathcal O_X^{\oplus k}$ is the old surjection composed with the surjective projection. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre] to this $(k+1)$-element family. At $z$ it gives an index $i$ with $z\in X_{h_i}$, meaning explicitly $(h_i)_z\notin\mathfrak m_zL_z$. By the defining criterion for zero in a quotient this says $h_i(z)\ne0$ in $L_z/\mathfrak m_zL_z$. Choose $t=h_i$.

source.place: Tags 01AM (modules-definition-globally-generated) and 01CY (modules-lemma-s-open), as carried by the cited fibre-criterion node; use its explicit germ-outside-maximal-ideal formulation, followed by the definition of the quotient.

proof.text: Define $v=s+ft$. Germ maps preserve addition and the module action, and passage to the quotient by $\mathfrak m_yL_y$ therefore gives $v(y)=s(y)+f(y)t(y)$ for every $y$. In the field $\kappa(z)$ of [def-weil-residue-field], the scalar $f(z)$ has an inverse. Since $s(z)=0$, if $v(z)=f(z)t(z)$ were zero, multiplying by $f(z)^{-1}$ would give $t(z)=0$, contrary to the choice of $t$. Hence $v(z)\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, proof, base case (global generation) and induction step (addition of sections); affine global generation follows Tags 01PB (properties-lemma-finite-type-module) and 01IA (schemes-lemma-quasi-coherent-affine).

proof.text: For each $x\in F$, substitute the assumed $f(x)=0$ into the same identity: $v(x)=s(x)+0\,t(x)=s(x)$. Together with $v(z)\ne0$ this proves both required clauses for the chosen global section $t$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_invertible_section_fibre_correction (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (F : Set X) (z : X) (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (f : Γ(X, ⊤)) (hs : residueValue s z trivial = 0) (hf : X.Γevaluation z f ≠ 0) (hF : ∀ x ∈ F, X.Γevaluation x f = 0) : ∃ t : Γ(L, ⊤), residueValue (s + f • t) z trivial ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x ∈ F, residueValue (s + f • t) x trivial = residueValue s x trivial
